data.name: Salomé
data.gender_notes: Salomé is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word shalom, meaning peace. In the Bible, Salomé was the name of the daughter of Herodias who requested the head of John the Baptist on a silver platter. The name Salomé carries the meaning “Peaceful, Quiet” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Salomé usually hope their child will grow to embody peaceful, quiet and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the desire for inner peace and calmness.
data.etymology: Salomé belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Peaceful, Quiet.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Salomé total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Salomé is a name that evokes intrigue and mystery, associated with ancient biblical stories and historical figures. It carries a rich cultural heritage, particularly within Christianity, and is often used to name girls who are treasured and blessed.
data.spiritual_significance: At its core, Salomé symbolizes peace and harmony. Just as the Bible tells us that the name shalom represents, Salomé carries a profound spiritual meaning. It serves as a reminder of the importance of inner peace and tranquility, emphasizing the pursuit of a balanced and composed life. Additionally, Salomé represents the power and wisdom of women, as demonstrated by her bold and resolute actions in the biblical narrative.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Salomé is the name of the enigmatic biblical woman who danced for King Herod and requested the head of John the Baptist. Her name symbolizes the power of seduction and desire, leading one to make bold requests from those in power. It also represents the complexity and mystery of womanhood, as Salomé's dance and request reveal both her allure and her destructive potential.

biblical_reference.note: Salome is mentioned in the New Testament as the mother of James and John, and the sister of Mary, mother of Jesus

historical_references.reference: Salomé is the name of the woman in the New Testament who danced for King Herod and asked for the head of John the Baptist.
